title: Minutes between sunrises: ISS vs. Earth's surface
notes: Because the ISS completes an orbit roughly every 93 minutes, it also passes from night into day about that often -- producing about 16 sunrises (and 16 sunsets) in one 24-hour period, versus 1 on the ground. 24 hours (1,440 minutes) divided by about 93 minutes per orbit is approximately 15.5, commonly rounded to about 16 sunrises a day (NASA).
